previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and chronic abdominal pain was admitted with worsening epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. She reported the symptoms began after an iron infusion and felt different from her usual gastroparesis flares. She had recently completed a course of cefpodoxime for a urinary tract infection. Initial labs showed leukocytosis, hyperglycemia, and normocytic anemia. A stool test confirmed Clostridium difficile infection. She was treated with intravenous fluids and started on oral metronidazole for a 10-day course. Her symptoms improved, she tolerated oral intake, and her abdominal tenderness resolved. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete her antibiotic course and follow up with her primary care provider.

Patient was recently for C. diff and was discharged on a 10 day 
course of Flagyl.  She did well until the morning of admission, 
when she woke up with a ""racing heart"" and shortness of breath.  
She did not have any chest pain.  Her daughter found her, and 
reports that she ""passed out"" four times in succession, but 
awoke on her own within seconds.  Patient then had acute onset 
abdominal pain, primarily epigastric, associated with nausea and 
3 episodes of green non-bloody vomit.  She continued to have 
abdominal pain.  Her diarrhea is unchanged since discharge.  She 
reports approximately 6 loose BMS per day.  Her blood sugars 
have been well-controlled.  Of note, patient and patient's 
daughter report that she has passed out before, usually in the 
context of severe abdominal pain/vomiting.

In the ED, initial vitals were: T 98.2, HR 108, BP 154/114, RR 
16, and SaO2 100% RA.  Labs were notable for WBC 17 (near 
baseline), H/H ___ (baseline), Cr 1.6, HCO3 21, AG 14, glucose 
224.  CXR showed no free air and KUB showed no 
megacolon/obstruction.  She was given Dilaudid, Zofran, and IVF. 
 On transfer to the floor, VS were T 98, HR 80, BP 134/70, RR 
18, and SaO2 100% RA.  
 
On the floor, patient was writhing in pain.  She also reported 
nausea and a ""migraine."
